result.title: Adversarial Multiplicity: Cherry-Picked Models and the Limits of Disclosure
result.summary: Predictive multiplicity -- where similarly accurate models disagree on individual predictions -- can be leveraged to optimize secondary metrics (e.g., fairness) without loss in predictive performance. However, exploiting multiplicity opens the opportunity for motivated parties (or coding agents gaming their objectives) to steer predictions toward their own ends, such as in litigation or consumer disputes with automated decision-making tools. In these adversarial multiplicity settings, we distinguish soft manipulation, where parties optimize over innocuous model choices (e.g., hyperparameter tuning, feature engineering), from hard manipulation, where parties directly perturb model parameters. We find a sufficiently flexible model can be manipulated to reverse any individual prediction with minimal change in predictive performance while passing black-box audits, making hard manipulation viable in most regulatory settings. Soft manipulation has smaller effects but can pass white-box audits requiring full access to code and data. Even aggregate estimates can be manipulated: a model's estimated effect of climate change on wildfires can be fully reversed by hard edits and soft search. We find the Reconcile algorithm typically resolves most disagreements between models, but more often in favor of the manipulator when the opposing model is chosen adversarially compared to at random. We map which manipulations can plausibly pass existing regulations and disclosure policies, and recommend mitigations such as pre-registration, proof of model training, sensitivity analyses, multi-metric evaluations, and committing to versioned public models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究「预测多重性」下的对抗操纵：区分软操纵（挑选超参、特征等无害模型选择）与硬操纵（直接扰动模型参数），考察当事方能否在几乎不损精度且通过黑箱/白箱审计的前提下翻转个体预测，并提出预注册、敏感性分析等缓解建议。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同等精度的模型在个体预测上任意分歧、行为审计难以识破」的结论，可能提示 LVR 中以行为或聚合指标判断 latent 是否真正使用视觉证据同样可被模型选择与微调操纵，可供核查评测可信度与因果归因设计。
